findings.issue_text: organization_context.member can be None for valid token/API-key authentication, so unconditionally accessing .has_global_access raises AttributeError even without optimized pagination
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on a datetime ordering key, causing TypeError when building cursors for nonempty optimized responses
The negative-offset branch passes negative slice indices to a Django QuerySet, causing an uncaught server error because Django rejects negative indexing
Subsequent optimized pages use the raw cursor value to filter a datetime column without converting it back to datetime, causing invalid or incorrect datetime comparisons

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Subsequent optimized pages use the raw cursor value to filter a datetime column without converting it back to datetime, causing invalid or incorrect datetime comparisons

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the OptimizedCursorPaginator class in the diff, the get_item_key method converts datetime values to integers using math.floor/ceil, and value_from_cursor simply returns cursor.value directly. When build_queryset is called with cursor_value (which comes from value_from_cursor), it would use this integer value to filter against a datetime column. The DateTimePaginator (not shown but referenced) likely has proper datetime conversion in value_from_cursor, but OptimizedCursorPaginator inherits from BasePaginator and only returns the raw cursor.value. Since this paginator is used for audit logs ordered by '-datetime', filtering with an integer instead of a datetime would cause incorrect comparisons.
